steps.what: Calculate efficiency from stored voltage, current, and fuel rate.
Check that this test's readings support the power output figure.

tasks.design: The {DATA_PLATFORM} calculates efficiency from stored voltage, current, and fuel rate, and only when all three belong to this test. Meter runtime is not counted. The fuel cell engineer checks that the inputs are this test's measurements and accepts the figure. A computed figure can still be the wrong test. Only the accepted figure is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: An efficiency was reported from a fuel rate that belonged to a different test.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored voltage, current, and fuel rate can be calculated. The engineer still has to check they are this test.
tasks.still_hard: A meter reading that was stored against the wrong test still has to be caught by the engineer.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer checks the inputs and accepts the figure. The calculation is arithmetic, and it can be wrong.
tasks.altitude: The check stays with the engineer. The figure is filed only after that version is accepted. Meter runtime is not treated as saved labour.

reach.task: Use an efficiency figure the fuel cell engineer has accepted.
reach.learn: A computed figure is not proof it was this test.

evidence.claim: Efficiency from stored voltage, current, and fuel rate is arithmetic. A figure can be computed and still be the wrong test.
Meter runtime is not the engineer's labour. Filing the figure before the engineer accepts that version would store a number nobody checked.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A fuel cell engineer in a mid-size European company. A stored record is not the experiment, and a draft is not the accepted design.

Fields: Voltage, current, and fuel rate, each already stored against this test id. Any one missing stops the calculation. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the fuel cell engineer finishes it by hand.
Native check: Calculate from the stored readings for this test. Do not type a reading from another test.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the fuel cell engineer.
unknowns: Whether fuel rate and current are stored on the same test row.
research_questions: Who attaches a reading to a test id before it can be used?

already_counted.description: Checking the inputs and accepting the figure stay with the engineer.

incremental.description: Drop readings whose test record has been withdrawn.

approvals.approved_version: test id and the voltage, current, and fuel rate the engineer accepted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The engineer still checks that the voltage, current, and fuel rate belong to this test and still accepts the figure. Only the arithmetic on those stored readings, and filing the accepted figure, is removed. Meter runtime is not counted. A missing reading saves none of the check.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the engineering schedule already shared with manufacturing.
Coordinate engineering schedules with manufacturing departments.

tasks.design: The {CALENDAR} shows the engineering or test schedule already stored. The fuel cell engineer coordinates it with manufacturing or other departments outside engineering. The screen does not move the other department. A schedule with no owner leaves the coordination with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: A test was moved on the engineering calendar and manufacturing still had the old day.
tasks.enabler_now: The stored schedule can be opened. The coordination still takes the conversation.
tasks.still_hard: A manufacturing constraint the schedule does not show still has to be heard.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer coordinates with the other department. The schedule is the record already stored.
tasks.altitude: The coordination stays in the conversation. The screen does not move another department's work.

reach.task: Say whether manufacturing can take the day the engineer is asking for.
reach.learn: A stored schedule is not their agreement.

evidence.claim: Opening a stored schedule is a lookup. It does not coordinate engineering with manufacturing.
Moving another department's work from a screen would skip the conversation this task is.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A fuel cell engineer in a mid-size European company. A stored record is not the experiment, and a draft is not the accepted design.

Fields: The schedule id already stored, including the department it was shared with. The screen does not change the other department's dates. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the fuel cell engineer finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the schedule on the calendar before the coordination meeting.
unknowns: Whether test schedules and engineering schedules share one calendar.
research_questions: Who is the manufacturing owner for a given test day?

already_counted.description: Coordinating the schedule stays with the engineer.

incremental.description: Drop schedule rows whose test has been cancelled.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The engineer still coordinates the engineering or test schedule with manufacturing and the other departments. Only opening a schedule that was already stored is removed. The screen does not move the other department, and a schedule with no owner saves none of the conversation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the part record proposed for production release.
Authorize release of these parts or subsystems for production.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store shows the part record proposed for production. The fuel cell engineer authorizes the release of the part, component, or subsystem. A stored part id is not the authorization, and the release is not an automatic decision. Only the release the engineer accepts is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: A part id was marked released before anyone authorized that part for production.
tasks.enabler_now: The part record can be opened. The release still has to be authorized by the engineer.
tasks.still_hard: A safety doubt the part record does not mention still stops the release until the engineer decides.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer authorizes the release. The part record is not the authorization.
tasks.altitude: The release stays a decision of the engineer. The file stores only the release that engineer accepted.

reach.task: Start production only from a release this engineer has accepted.
reach.learn: A part id is not a release.

evidence.claim: Opening a part record is a lookup. It does not authorize a part, a component, or a subsystem for production.
A production release of a fuel cell part is a safety decision and is not an automatic decision. The signing engineer stays responsible.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A fuel cell engineer in a mid-size European company. A stored record is not the experiment, and a draft is not the accepted design.

Fields: The part id and the subsystem id already stored. The release sentence is not added by the screen. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the fuel cell engineer finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the part record in the document store before the authorization. Do not mark it released from the id alone.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the fuel cell engineer.
unknowns: Whether parts and subsystems use the same release record.
research_questions: Which safety checks must be on the part record before an engineer will consider a release?

already_counted.description: Authorizing the release stays with the engineer.

incremental.description: Drop release drafts whose part record has been withdrawn.

approvals.approved_version: part id, subsystem id, and the release sentence the engineer accepted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The engineer still authorizes the release of the part, component, or subsystem for production. Only opening the part record, and filing the release already accepted, is removed. A part id saves none of that safety decision, and the release is not automatic.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show stored power, cost, and impact figures for this design.
Evaluate hydrogen designs for power output and environmental impact.

tasks.design: The {DATA_PLATFORM} shows power output, system cost, and environmental impact only when those figures are already stored for this design. The fuel cell engineer evaluates the new hydrogen or non-hydrogen design. A missing figure is not invented. Only the evaluation the engineer accepts is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: An environmental impact was stated for a design that had no stored impact figure.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored figures can be opened. The evaluation still belongs to the engineer.
tasks.still_hard: A design whose cost or impact was never stored still has to be judged without a invented number.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer evaluates the design. A missing figure is not filled in.
tasks.altitude: The evaluation stays with the engineer. It is filed only after that version is accepted.

reach.task: Read an evaluation the fuel cell engineer has accepted.
reach.learn: A blank impact field is not a low impact.

evidence.claim: Opening stored power, cost, and impact figures is a lookup. It does not evaluate the design.
Filing an evaluation before the engineer accepts that version would store a judgement nobody made, including an impact nobody stored.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: A fuel cell engineer in a mid-size European company. A stored record is not the experiment, and a draft is not the accepted design.

Fields: Power output, system cost, and environmental impact, each already stored for this design id. A missing figure is not invented. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the fuel cell engineer finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the figures from the data platform before the evaluation. Do not type an impact that is not stored.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the fuel cell engineer.
unknowns: Whether hydrogen and non-hydrogen designs share one figure record.
research_questions: Who is allowed to store an environmental impact figure for a design?

already_counted.description: Evaluating the design stays with the engineer.

incremental.description: Drop figures whose design record has been withdrawn.

approvals.approved_version: design id and the evaluation sentence the engineer accepted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The engineer still evaluates power output, system cost, and environmental impact of the new design. Only opening figures already stored, and filing the evaluation already accepted, is removed. A missing figure saves none of the evaluation, and none is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The fuel cell engineer still checks the efficiency figure, still coordinates the schedule, still authorizes a release, and still evaluates a new design. A stored number can be shown. It does not make the decision.
reach: Manufacturing planners read a schedule, and this job learns the screen does not move their work.
Production leads a release only after this engineer has accepted it, and a part id is not that release.
skills_to_grow: Check that an efficiency figure uses this test's own measurements.
Coordinate a schedule in the conversation with the other department.
Authorize a production release as a safety decision, never as an automatic file.
role.ambitious_version: Efficiency checks, schedule talks, production releases, and design evaluations stay with the engineer. Stored measurements and part records only show what was already written.
